To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the Upf1p helicase core reveals an overall architecture that includes a single‐stranded DNA‐binding channel, a likely ssRNA‐interacting channel, and a conformational change that can explain how ssRNA binding is destabilized upon ATP binding.
the structure of human Upf‐1 helicase reveals a novel RNA‐binding channel and a mechanism of ATP‐dependent RNA binding.

the structure of the catalytically active form of human Upf‐1p is similar to that of the RecA family of helicases, that the N‐terminus of Upf‐1 is involved in the binding of Upf2p, and that ATP binding and hydro lysis promote a conformational change that alters the ssRNA‐binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of NMD, which plays an important role in gene expression regulation and disease.
the structure and function of the Upf1 protein and its involvement in the Nonsense Mediated Decay (NMD) pathway.
the structure, function and evolution of the human nonsense‐mediated mRNA surveillance protein Upf1p.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Upf1p is a hexameric helicase, which is likely to bind ssRNA in the RecA‐like N‐terminal domain.
Upf1p has a RecA‐like structure and is likely to function as a hexameric ring.
the structure of human Upf 1 is a novel member of SF1, which contains two RecA‐type domains with an additional N‐terminal domain and a C‐terminal domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the crystal structure of the human Upf‐1 core protein, and we have used this structure to understand the mechanism of action of this protein.
the structural data support the notion that Upf1p is a ssRNA helicase and that the conformational changes observed in Upf1p are likely important for its function.
the structure of human Upf‐1 helicase provides insights into the mechanism of NMD and the structure and function of SF1 helicases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structural and biochemical analyses of Upf1p have provided a framework for understanding how the Upf1p helicase core might interact with RNA to promote transitions between different RNA structures.

Upf1p is a highly versatile enzyme that is capable of utilizing ATP hydrolysis for multiple purposes, and that the Upf1p helicase core can function as a ssRNA‐binding protein, a helicase, and an NMD‐promoting factor.
Upf1p is a highly flexible protein, with a structure that is likely to be able to accommodate a variety of RNA and protein interactions.
